Paki-paliwanag po ang Artikulo 1210 ng Kodigo Sibil tungkol sa pagkakaiba ng indivisibility at solidarity.

Sinasabi ng Artikulo 1210 na magkaiba ang indivisibility at solidarity. Ang indivisibility ay tungkol sa bagay o prestasyon na hindi maaaring hatiin, tulad ng paghahatid ng isang partikular na sasakyan. Ang solidarity naman ay tungkol sa relasyon ng maraming may utang o nagpautang—kung ang bawat may utang ay mananagot sa buong obligasyon o ang bawat nagpautang ay maaaring humingi ng buong pagtupad. Maaaring indivisible ang obligasyon ngunit hindi solidary: halimbawa, dalawang may utang ang may obligasyong maghatid ng isang kotse, ngunit hindi sila solidary, kaya bawat isa ay mananagot lamang sa kanyang bahagi; subalit dahil hindi mahahati ang kotse, kailangang humingi ng pagtupad mula sa kanilang dalawa nang magkasama, o kung kusang ihahatid ng isa ang buong kotse, maaari siyang maningil ng reimbursement mula sa isa pa. Sa kabilang banda, maaaring solidary ang obligasyon ngunit divisible: halimbawa, tatlong solidary na may utang ang may pagkakautang na P90,000; dahil sa solidarity, sinuman sa kanila ay maaaring pilitin na magbayad ng buong P90,000, kahit na ang pera ay divisible. Nililinaw ng artikulo na ang isang katangian ay hindi awtomatikong nagbibigay ng isa pa.

Can you explain Article 660 of the Philippine Civil Code about exterior signs contrary to the easement of party wall?

Article 660 of the Philippine Civil Code lists exterior signs that indicate a dividing wall is NOT a party wall but is exclusively owned by one property owner. These signs include: (1) windows or openings in the wall; (2) the wall being straight and plumb on one side but slanting or projecting on the lower part on the other; (3) the entire wall built within one property's boundaries; (4) the wall bearing beams, floors, or roof frame of one building but not the other; (5) the coping shedding water onto only one estate; (6) stepping stones projecting from one side only; (7) lands enclosed by fences or hedges adjoining unenclosed lands. In all these cases, the wall, fence, or hedge is presumed to belong exclusively to the owner whose property has the sign in its favor.

### 📚 Governing Statutory Basis

However, because the land value (₱5 million) is considerably more than the value of your house (₱300,000), the landowner cannot force you to buy the land. [Art. 448].

### 💡 Application to Facts
In this case, if the landowner does not choose to appropriate the house after paying proper indemnity, you as the builder must pay reasonable rent for the use of the land. The parties should try to agree on the lease terms; if you cannot agree, the court will fix the terms.

STATUTORY TEXT: Merger which takes place in the person of the principal debtor or creditor benefits the guarantors. Confusion which takes place in the person of any of the latter does not extinguish the obligation.

I was a guarantor for my cousin's business loan. Last month, my cousin transferred the business to me, including all his debts, so now I am the one responsible to pay the loan. The bank says I am now the principal debtor and must pay. But I thought since I was the guarantor, the obligation might be extinguished because I am both debtor and guarantor? Is the loan still valid according to Article 1276?

Your former guarantee is merged into your new principal obligation, but the debt itself survives.

### 📚 Governing Statutory Basis
Under Article 1276, confusion or merger of rights occurs when the characters of creditor and debtor are merged in the same person. If this occurs in the person of the principal debtor or creditor, the obligation is extinguished and benefits the guarantors. However, if confusion occurs in the person of a guarantor, it does not extinguish the principal obligation. [Art. 1276].

### 💡 Application to Facts
In your case, you were originally a guarantor, and now you have also assumed the role of principal debtor by taking over the business and its debts. This is a confusion in the person of the guarantor, which does not extinguish the obligation. The loan remains valid and enforceable; you are now the principal debtor and must pay the debt.

- **Competent Court / Jurisdiction**: Municipal Trial Court (MTC / MeTC / MTCC / MCTC) if monetary claim does not exceed ₱2,000,000 (Small Claims Court if ≤ ₱1,000,000 pursuant to SC Small Claims Rules); Regional Trial Court (RTC) if claim exceeds ₱2,000,000 or if incapable of pecuniary estimation pursuant to RA 11576.

Can my husband donate our condo unit to me while we are married?

Under Article 133 of the Philippine Civil Code, every donation between spouses during the marriage is void by operation of law. This means spouses cannot legally transfer real property or significant assets to each other as inter vivos gifts while both are alive. The purpose of this rule is to protect the family estate and prevent one spouse from exercising undue influence over the other.
What if it's just a watch or jewelry given on my birthday or our wedding anniversary?

That is a recognized legal exception! Article 133 expressly allows moderate gifts given between spouses on occasions of family rejoicing, such as birthdays, anniversaries, or holiday celebrations. As long as the watch or piece of jewelry is moderate in value relative to your family's financial standing, it is completely valid and legal.

Legal po ba ang bentahan ng lupa kung verbal o salitaan lang ang kasunduan?

Ayon sa Artikulo 1403(2) ng Kodigo Sibil (Statute of Frauds), ang kasunduan sa pagbebenta ng lupa o real property ay dapat nakasulat upang maipatupad sa korte. Kung ito ay purong salitaan lamang at wala pang aksyon o bayaran, ito ay 'unenforceable'—ibig sabihin, may bisa ang kasunduan sa pagitan ninyo pero hindi mo mapipilit ang kabilang panig sa korte kung magbago ang kanyang isip.
Paano po kung nagbayad na ako ng kalahati ng halaga at tinanggap naman ng nagbenta?

Kung nagbayad ka na ng partial payment at tinanggap ito ng nagbenta, nagkaroon na ng 'partial execution' (bahagyang pagtupad). Sa ilalim ng Artikulo 1405, ang kontrata ay hindi na saklaw ng Statute of Frauds. Dahil dito, maaari mo nang obligahin ang nagbenta sa hukuman na isakatuparan ang bentahan at gumawa ng pormal na Deed of Absolute Sale para mailipat ang titulo sa iyong pangalan.
